vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: here-now
Version: 1.14.0

The 'here-now' skill is a legitimate tool for deploying static files and directories to the here.now hosting service. The bash script (publish.sh) implements a standard three-step upload process (create, upload, finalize) using pre-signed URLs and includes security best practices, such as a safety guard that prevents sending the API key to non-default base URLs. The instructions in SKILL.md correctly guide the agent through authentication and deployment workflows, and the use of external documentation (here.now/docs) is a standard practice for maintaining up-to-date agent capabilities.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and optional credentials are consistent with a static-site publishing tool; it needs local files and may write a local credentials/state file and upload data to the here.now API, which matches its stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (instant static hosting) match the provided script and runtime instructions. The optional HERENOW_API_KEY and ~/.herenow/credentials file are appropriate for a service that supports authenticated, permanent sites. The script's network calls target here.now endpoints and the file I/O (building a manifest, reading files) is required to upload site contents.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the agent to run scripts/publish.sh, read the working directory, compute hashes, and upload files — all expected for deployment. They also instruct storing an API key in ~/.herenow/credentials and writing .herenow/state.json in the working directory; the docs explicitly tell the agent to save the API key itself ('do not ask the user to run it manually'), which expands the agent's responsibilities to writing local credential files. This is coherent for a publishing tool but worth noting because it involves writing sensitive data to disk under agent control.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No installation step (instruction-only plus an included publish script). No downloads or external installers. Risk from install mechanism is low because nothing is fetched/installed by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables are declared in the registry; SKILL.md reasonably documents a single optional HERENOW_API_KEY and an optional credentials file. The script also respects a safety guard refusing to send an API key to a non-default base URL unless explicitly overridden. The amount and type of environment/file access requested is proportional to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes a per-site state cache (.herenow/state.json) to the working directory and can store an API key in ~/.herenow/credentials for persistent authenticated publishes. always:false and normal autonomous invocation are set. Writing local credential/state files is expected, but users should be aware the agent may create/modify those files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it will read files/directories you point it at, compute hashes/manifests, and upload them to the here.now API. If you authenticate, the agent/script will store an API key at ~/.herenow/credentials and will create .herenow/state.json in the working directory. Before installing or using it: (1) only publish non-sensitive test files until you trust the service; (2) if you are uncomfortable with the agent writing a credentials file, do not provide an API key and use anonymous publishes (they expire in 24h); (3) review scripts/publish.sh (it is included) and confirm the BASE_URL is the expected service endpoint; (4) be aware the agent may ask for an email and one-time sign-in code to obtain an API key and will be instructed to save that key locally — allow writing only if you trust here.now. If you want stronger assurance, ask the skill author for hosting/service documentation and a verified homepage before using authenticated publishes.
llm.findings: [no_pre_scan_signals] expected: Static scan reported no pre-scan injection signals. That matches an instruction-heavy skill with a simple shell script; absence of findings is not proof of safety but is unsurprising here.
